opportunity.title: Scalable GEOINT Architecture IT Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support
opportunity.description: Request for Proposal W50NH9-27-R-A006 for Scalable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture IT Contractor Manpower Equivalent support for U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM). Proposals due Nov 13, 2026 with a proposal validity of at least 240 days. Period of performance: one 30-day transition-in, a 12-month base, four 12-month options and one six-month option. Estimated award date Jan 11, 2027. Primarily time and materials, evaluated on a best value trade-off basis.

rationale.point: The opportunity seeks scalable GEOINT architecture IT CME support for Army INSCOM (claim #1), which aligns with Atlas Federal's DoD IT prime contract experience and Top Secret facility clearance, though the firm lacks explicit GEOINT past performance.
INSCOM's contracting office (ACC-DTA) has Virginia offices (claim #2), matching Atlas Federal's VA headquarters and place-of-performance flexibility, reducing geographic risk.

BAE Systems' $75M award for next-gen geospatial intelligence (claim #3) signals strong incumbent competition and a contract scale exceeding Atlas Federal's typical $5M–$60M prime range, suggesting a teaming strategy may be needed.

risks: No demonstrated GEOINT or geospatial intelligence past performance in company profile
Median top award value ($152M) far exceeds Atlas Federal's historical prime contract ceiling ($60M)
Large business status means no set-aside protection; must compete full-and-open against established primes like BAE Systems
nextSteps: Review full RFP W50NH9-27-R-A006 for specific GEOINT technical requirements and labor categories
Identify potential teaming partners with proven GEOINT/geospatial intelligence capabilities
Assess whether Atlas Federal's 150 cleared staff and FedRAMP Moderate authorization meet INSCOM's security and compliance needs
Develop pricing model competitive for CME manpower-equivalent structure
